alt: Two cards define liberalism and nationalism, held down by Metternich's system (the Congress of Vienna, the Carlsbad Decrees, Austrian troops in Italy). Below, the economic trigger: potato blight from 1845, poor harvests in 1846 and a slump in 1847 led to dear bread and unemployment in 1848.
caption: Liberal and nationalist ideas met an economic crisis in 1848.

alt: Four lanes on one time scale from January 1848 to August 1849. France: the king abdicates (February), the June Days, Louis Napoleon elected (December); his coup came only in 1851. Italy: Palermo (January), Milan's Five Days, Custoza, Novara and the fall of Venice (August 1849). Germany: the Berlin rising, the Frankfurt Parliament and the crown refused (April 1849). Austrian Empire: Vienna and Metternich's fall, Prague, Vienna retaken and Hungary crushed (August 1849).
caption: Every revolution rose in early 1848 and was over by late 1849.

after: ## Did the revolutions have anything in common?
alt: A table of five common features with examples: liberal demands, nationalist aims, an economic trigger, middle-class urban leaders and early success followed by collapse within about 18 months. Two differences: France was already a nation, and in the Austrian Empire nationalism split the revolution.
caption: Shared causes and pattern, but different aims in France and the Austrian Empire.

after: ## Why did most of the revolutions fail?
alt: A hub with "most revolutions fail" at the centre and six reasons around it: rulers kept their armies (highlighted), revolutionaries were divided, nationalities clashed, peasants lost interest, foreign powers intervened, and leadership was weak.
caption: Division weakened the revolutions; loyal armies defeated them.

alt: A balance. Little change: monarchs restored by 1849-50, Austria back in control, no united Germany, liberals jailed or exiled. Lasting change: the end of serfdom in Austria, French male suffrage, Piedmont's constitution, a Prussian parliament, and lessons learned by Cavour and Bismarck.
caption: Rulers returned, but serfdom, suffrage and Piedmont's constitution lasted.

alt: Two factor cards, division (the June Days) and force (Vienna retaken, Hungary crushed), lead to a judgement: the armies decided, and division explains why there was little resistance when the troops returned.
caption: Link the factors: show how one made the other effective.
